hints: Calculate the loss of gravitational potential energy of A as it falls $0.75\text{ m}$: $\Delta PE_A = mg(0.75) = 7.5m$.

Calculate the gain of gravitational potential energy of B ascending $0.75\text{ m}$ along the plane ($
in \theta = 0.6$): $\Delta PE_B = 3g(0.75 \times 0.6) = 13.5\text{ J}$, and work against resistance: $\frac{10}{3} \times 0.75 = 2.5\text{ J}$.
Set up the work-energy balance: $\Delta PE_A - \Delta PE_B - W_{\text{res}} = \frac{1}{2}(m + 3)(2^2)$ and solve for $m$.
walkthrough: Apply the work-energy principle to the connected system from rest until particle A strikes the ground after descending $h = 0.75\text{ m}$.

Step 1: Potential energy changes:
- Particle A of mass $m$ falls vertically through $0.75\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{lost, A}} = m g h = m \times 10 \times 0.75 = 7.5m\text{ J}$$
- Particle B of mass $3\text{ kg}$ moves $0.75\text{ m}$ up the plane inclined at $\theta$ where $\sin \theta = 0.6$. The vertical rise is $h_B = 0.75 \sin \theta = 0.75 \times 0.6 = 0.45\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{gained, B}} = m_B g h_B = 3 \times 10 \times 0.45 = 13.5\text{ J}$$

Step 2: Work done against the resistance force:
A constant resistance of $\frac{10}{3}\text{ N}$ opposes the motion of B over distance $0.75\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{res}} = R_B \times d = \frac{10}{3} \times 0.75 = \frac{7.5}{3} = 2.5\text{ J}$$

Step 3: Kinetic energy of the system:
Both particles start from rest and reach a final speed of $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$KE_{\text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}(m_A + m_B)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(m + 3)(2^2) = 2(m + 3) = 2m + 6\text{ J}$$

Step 4: Set up and solve the work-energy equation:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{lost, A}} - \Delta PE_{\text{gained, B}} - W_{\text{res}} = KE_{\text{final}}$$
$$7.5m - 13.5 - 2.5 = 2m + 6$$
$$7.5m - 16 = 2m + 6$$
$$5.5m = 22$$
$$m = \frac{22}{5.5} = 4\text{ kg}$$
